diagnosis.root_cause: Ledger::completeNativeDraw currently treats any mutation during native Draw as a failed GPU transaction. A successful hooked Flush from D3DXSprite::Draw itself changes that serial, causing the returning successful texture draw to be discarded as an exact +TIME/GOAL owner.
diagnosis.original_evidence: The live original DrawDest calls Draw_hk.stdcall then completeNativeDraw against the pre-call snapshot. FlushDest calls completeNativeFlush, which clears the command ledger on success and advances mutationSerial before outer Draw returns.
source_trace: Original E8 and Sumo queue assign exact StageExtensionTime and result producer before native ID3DXSprite::Draw.
A D3DX texture transition can internally invoke native Flush, clearing prior commands in the live ledger without ending the same Begin generation.
The outer successful Draw then adds the next texture's first command, whose exact ownership must survive to Flush/End and R84 eye classification.
alternatives_rejected: Unknown, mixed, failed or foreign D3DX work is not promoted, and no per-Draw global Flush is introduced.
No claim that this particular internal texture transition has yet been captured in Quest3 gameplay; hardware confirmation remains outstanding.
diagnosis.eye_ownership: Loss of the exact ScreenHud producer can route +TIME sprite or numeric glyph into generic overlay behavior rather than R84's finite binocular HUD plane.
